rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1, 3 and Table 4 - the authors use their own telemetry data from 627 hydrants (228,855 daily observations, 2015) in Sector II of the Canal del Zujar Irrigation District to train and test decision trees optimised by NSGA-II, reporting confusion matrices for the test set.
rows.notes: The study does not report any result on water conservation or water-loss reduction. Its own result is the classification accuracy of a model that predicts, one day ahead, whether a farmer will irrigate (positive events 68-100 %, negative events 93-100 % correctly classified on a held-out 20 % test set). Benefits for energy efficiency, pumping-station operation and management are stated only as potential uses in the Introduction and Conclusions, not measured. The model predicts farmer behaviour for district managers rather than advising farmers when to schedule irrigation; the claimed water-saving effect is downstream of what is tested, so Q2 is 'no' and the study is upstream. The authors do note a limitation (class imbalance makes positive events harder to predict; inputs must be redefined for each area) but this concerns prediction accuracy, not the claimed water-conservation effect, so it does not count under Q8.

notes: Full text appears complete (post-print with tables and figure captions). Study is a single-season, single-sector modelling exercise in Spain; no water-use or energy outcomes were measured.
